name: TransNormerLLM: A Faster and Better Large Language Model with Improved TransNormer
problem: Linear-attention LLMs were claimed to beat softmax attention on accuracy, but in practice suffered attention dilution, unstable training, and no practical inference path.
mechanism: Evolves TransNormer with five changes: (1) LRPE - a relative position embedding - combined with exponential decay to prevent attention dilution while retaining global token interaction; (2) Lightning Attention to accelerate the linear attention kernel (>2x runtime, 4x less memory); (3) a gating mechanism for training stability; (4) a new tensor-normalisation scheme; (5) an inference algorithm that keeps decode speed constant regardless of sequence length, plus a model-parallel schema for large clusters.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claims (abstract), component-wise with the comparison named in each case: Lightning Attention accelerates linear attention by more than 2x runtime and reduces memory 4x (baseline: the linear-attention formulation it replaces); the tensor-normalisation scheme yields over 20% acceleration; trained model sizes 385M, 1B and 7B on a self-collected corpus, matching SOTA Transformer-based LLMs while being faster.
notes: arXiv ID 2307.14995 verified via abs-page meta tags on 2026-10-03; title matches. VENUE - and this is a correction to a widely repeated citation: TransNormerLLM is NOT ICLR 2024. OpenReview forum OROKjdAfjs (authors Qin, Li, Sun, Sun - matching the paper) returns venueid='ICLR.cc/2024/Conference/Rejected_Submission', venue='Submitted to ICLR 2024'. venue=arxiv-preprint on evidence, with this note. adoption=abandoned, and the basis is a live check: official repo OpenNLPLab/TransnormerLLM last pushed 2024-01-23 with 255 stars; no TransNormer entry in vLLM's model registry, SGLang's 248-file models directory, or transformers models/; and the sibling lightning-attention repo is equally stalled. The paper's own 'seamless deployment on large-scale clusters enabling 175B-parameter expansion' is a design intent in the paper, not a shipped deployment - worth stating because the abstract reads as if it were done.
